extracted.intended_audience: drug applicants, NDA/ANDA holders, regulatory affairs professionals, and pharmaceutical manufacturers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedural standards for submitting amendments and supplements to NDAs (including 505(b)(2) applications), categorizing changes (major/moderate/minor), required contents and timing of supplements/annual reports, change-of-ownership procedures, and postmarketing adverse drug experience review and reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information required for an ACNU in nonprescription ANDAs
rubrics_metrics.description: If an ANDA proposes an additional condition of nonuse (ACNU) for a nonprescription drug product, the submission must include: (i) a description showing that the purpose of the proposed ACNU is the same as the ACNU for its reference listed drug (RLD); (ii) information demonstrating that the key elements of the ACNU are the same as the key elements of the ACNU for its RLD; and (iii) a description of the specific way(s) the ACNU is operationalized (or, if operationalized differently, information showing the different operationalization achieves the same purpose and the differences are otherwise acceptable in an ANDA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant believes operationalization is the same as the RLD, include information to demonstrate that. If different, include data/explanation showing the alternative achieves the same purpose and is acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACNU as a meaningful difference for simultaneous marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: An ACNU constitutes a meaningful difference between a nonprescription drug product and a prescription drug product such that both may be simultaneously marketed even if there is not another meaningful difference making the nonprescription product safe and effective without practitioner supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACNU can permit simultaneous marketing despite otherwise-identical products (contrast with differences like active ingredient, indication, strength, route, dosage form, or patient population).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of an amendment to an unapproved NDA
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may submit an amendment to an original NDA, a supplement to an approved NDA, or a resubmission that has been filed under §314.101 but is not yet approved; FDA generally assumes submission means applicant believes the filing can be approved as submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments are permissible prior to approval; other timing/extension rules (see major/minor amendment rules) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major amendment timing and review-cycle extension (original NDA/efficacy supplements/resubmissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a major amendment within 3 months of the end of the initial review cycle constitutes agreement by the applicant to extend the initial review cycle by 3 months; FDA may defer review until the subsequent review cycle; the initial review cycle may be extended only once due to submission of a major amendment; FDA may at its discretion review subsequent major amendments during the (extended) initial review cycle or defer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major amendment submitted more than 3 months before the end of the initial review cycle will not extend the cycle (FDA may review or defer). A major amendment to a manufacturing supplement within 2 months of the end of the initial review cycle constitutes agreement to extend by 2 months (with similar deferral/one-time-extension rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of non-major amendments on review cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of an amendment that is not a major amendment will not extend the initial review cycle; FDA may, at its discretion, review such an amendment during the initial review cycle or defer review until the subsequent review cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish major vs non-major when considering impact on timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major amendment content limitation (new indications/claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: A major amendment may not include data to support an indication or claim that was not included in the original NDA, supplement, or resubmission, but it may include data to support a minor modification of an indication or claim that was included originally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use a major amendment to add wholly new indications or claims not in the original submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on amendments where exclusivity exists (deemed withdrawal)
rubrics_metrics.description: An unapproved NDA may not be amended if (i) a previous NDA for the drug has been approved and granted a period of exclusivity that has not expired; (ii) the applicant seeks to amend to include a published report of an investigation entitled to exclusivity; (iii) the applicant has not obtained a right of reference or use to that investigation; and (iv) the report would be essential to approval of the unapproved NDA. Submission of such an amendment will cause the unapproved NDA to be deemed withdrawn and the amendment will be considered a resubmission, which may not be accepted except as provided in section 505(c)(3)(E)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the four conditions all apply, do not submit the amendment — it will cause deemed withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field copy requirement for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must submit a field copy of each amendment to a section of the NDA described in §314.50(d)(1) and include a statement certifying that a field copy of the amendment has been sent to the applicant's home FDA district office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include field copy and certification with each applicable amendment submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on amending a 505(b)(2) to seek approval of a different drug
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may not amend a 505(b)(2) application to seek approval of a drug that is a 'different drug' from the drug in the original submission; a 'different drug' is one modified to have a different active ingredient, route, dosage form, or excipients that requires either a separate clinical study to establish safety/effectiveness or (for topical products) a separate in vivo demonstration of bioequivalence. An applicant may, however, amend to seek approval of a different strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a new application rather than amending 505(b)(2) if the change meets the 'different drug' definition (except for strength changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent certification/recertification requirements for amendments to 505(b)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment to a 505(b)(2) application must contain an appropriate patent certification or statement described in §314.50(i), or a recertification for a previously submitted paragraph IV certification, if approval is sought for: (i) a new indication or condition of use; (ii) a new strength; (iii) other than minor changes in formulation; or (iv) a change in the physical form or crystalline structure of the active ingredient. If the amendment does not contain a patent certification/statement, the applicant must verify the change is not one of these types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure appropriate patent information is provided when amendments seek the listed types of approval; otherwise include verification the change is not of those types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of an unapproved application by the applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may withdraw an application that is not yet approved at any time by notifying FDA in writing. If FDA has identified deficiencies by receipt of such notice, the agency will list such deficiencies in its acknowledgement letter. The decision to withdraw is without prejudice to refiling. FDA will retain the application and provide a copy to the applicant on request under the fee schedule in §20.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal does not prevent refiling; FDA will document known deficiencies and retains the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: General change notification requirement for approved NDAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided (e.g., by grants under §201.26), the applicant must notify FDA about each change in each condition established in an approved NDA beyond the variations already provided; the notice must fully describe the change and, depending on type, be made via supplement (paragraphs (b) or (c)) or in the annual report (paragraph (d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine correct reporting pathway (prior approval supplement, 30-day supplement, or annual report) depending on potential impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to assess effects of manufacturing changes before distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The NDA holder must assess the effects of the change before distributing a drug product made with a manufacturing change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform and document assessments supporting that the change does not adversely affect identity, strength, quality, purity, or potency as they relate to safety/effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to revise promotional labeling promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must promptly revise all promotional labeling and advertising to make it consistent with any labeling change implemented according to supplement/annual report provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure promotional materials reflect any approved or implemented labeling changes without delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major changes requiring prior approval (definition and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior-approval supplement must be submitted for any change in drug substance, drug product, production process, quality controls, equipment, or facilities that has a substantial potential to have an adverse effect on identity, strength, quality, purity, or potency as these factors relate to safety/effectiveness. Examples include (but are not limited to): changes in qualitative/quantitative formulation (except those in (c)/(d)), changes requiring bioequivalence or equivalence studies under part 320, changes affecting sterility assurance, changes in synthesis/manufacture that may affect impurity profile or physico-chemical properties, specified labeling changes (see §314.70(b)(2)(v)), container-closure changes that control delivery or affect impurity profile, specified biologic/complex-product manufacturing changes, and changes to NDAs subject to validity assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the change appears to have substantial potential to adversely affect critical attributes, submit a prior-approval supplement and include required supporting information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information required in a prior-approval supplement
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for submissions under paragraph (e), a prior-approval supplement must contain: (i) a detailed description of the proposed change; (ii) the drug product(s) involved; (iii) the manufacturing site(s)/area(s) affected; (iv) description of methods used and studies performed to assess effects of the change; (v) the data from such studies; (vi) for certain products (natural products, recombinant proteins, complexes with monoclonal antibodies) relevant validation protocols and list of relevant SOPs; and (vii) for sterilization process/test methodologies, relevant validation protocols and SOPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full technical justification and raw data so FDA can assess safety/effectiveness impact prior to approval for distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited review request procedure for supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may ask FDA to expedite review of a supplement for public health reasons or if delay would impose extraordinary hardship; such supplements should be plainly marked: 'Prior Approval Supplement-Expedited Review Requested.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark plainly to request expedited review; justification should explain public health need or extraordinary hardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderate changes (30-day supplement) definition and process
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplement must be submitted at least 30 days prior to distribution for any change that has a moderate potential to have an adverse effect on identity, strength, quality, purity, or potency. The supplement must provide a full explanation of the basis for the change, identify the date the change will be made, and be labeled 'Supplement—Changes Being Effected in 30 Days' (or 'Supplement—Changes Being Effected' where applicable). Pending approval, distribution may begin not less than 30 days after FDA's receipt unless FDA within 30 days informs the applicant the change requires prior approval or that required information is missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the same supporting information listed for prior-approval supplements (detailed description, methods, data, etc.). If FDA objects within 30 days, do not distribute until issue resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency-designated categories allowing immediate distribution upon receipt of supplement
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may designate categories of changes for which the holder of an approved NDA may commence distribution of the drug product upon receipt by FDA of a supplement for the change. Examples include: additions to specifications or changes in methods/controls that increase assurance of critical attributes; changes in size/shape of container for nonsterile products (except solids); labeling changes to reflect newly acquired information that strengthen safety information or delete false claims; or any labeling change FDA specifically requests be submitted under this provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If FDA designates a change category as eligible, distribution may begin upon receipt of supplement rather than waiting for approval—check agency designations and follow labeling requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA authority to order cessation of distribution upon disapproval
rubrics_metrics.description: If FDA disapproves the supplemental NDA, it may order the manufacturer to cease distribution of the drug product(s) made with the manufacturing change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to halt distribution if supplement disapproved; maintain compliance documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor changes to be documented in annual report (definition and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes that have a minimal potential to adversely affect identity, strength, quality, purity, or potency must be documented in the next annual report. Examples include changes made to comply with official compendium updates (consistent with FDA requirements), deletion/reduction of a color-only ingredient, replacement of equipment with same design/operating principles, certain container size/shape changes for nonsterile solids, container-closure changes based on equivalency showing, extension of expiration dating based on full shelf-life data from NDA-approved protocol, addition/revision of alternative analytical procedures that provide same/increased assurance, minor code imprint changes, labeling changes about how supplied (not dosage strength), and editorial/minor labeling changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and include details in annual report per §314.81(b)(2); do not treat these as prior-approval or 30-day supplements unless otherwise specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of annual report for minor changes
rubrics_metrics.description: For changes documented in the annual report, the applicant must include: (i) a statement that effects of the change have been assessed; (ii) a full description of the manufacturing and controls changes, including manufacturing site(s)/area(s); (iii) the date each change was implemented; (iv) data from studies/tests performed to assess effects; and (v) for certain products (natural products, recombinant proteins, complexes with monoclonal antibodies, sterilization processes), a cross-reference to relevant validation protocols and/or SOPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual reports must be sufficiently detailed to allow FDA to evaluate the implemented minor changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocols for specified manufacturing changes
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may submit protocols describing specific tests/studies and acceptance criteria to demonstrate lack of adverse effect for specified manufacturing changes. Protocols not included in the approved NDA, or changes to an approved protocol, must be submitted as a supplement requiring approval prior to distribution of a product produced with the change. If FDA approves the supplement, the approved protocol may justify a reduced reporting category for that type of change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use protocols to streamline future reporting categories, but submit and obtain approval for protocols not already in the approved NDA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent information and claimed exclusivity when submitting supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must comply with patent information requirements under section 505(c)(2) and §314.53. If claiming exclusivity under §314.108 upon approval of a supplement for a change, the applicant must include with its supplement the information required under §314.50(j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include required patent/exclusivity information with supplements when applicable to preserve rights and meet statutory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for submission of supplements (who may submit and copy requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the applicant may submit a supplement. All procedures/actions that apply to an application under §314.50 also apply to supplements, except the information required is limited to that needed to support the change. A supplement must contain an archival copy and a review copy that include an application form, appropriate technical sections, samples, and labeling; except that a supplement for a change other than labeling must also contain a field copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure correct copies (archival, review, field when required) and include only information needed to support the change, following §314.50 procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in ownership of an application — required notifications and commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: When transferring ownership of an application: (a) the former owner must submit a letter or other document stating that all rights have been transferred; (b) the new owner must submit a signed application form and a letter containing: (i) commitment to agreements/promises/conditions made by former owner in the application; (ii) effective date of change; and (iii) either a statement that the new owner has a complete copy of the approved application (including required records) or a request for a copy from FDA (which FDA will provide under §20.45). The new owner must advise FDA about any change in conditions in the approved application under §314.70, though certain labeling changes (brand or name of manufacturer/packer/distributor) may be advised in the next annual report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete documentation at transfer and ensure continuity of commitments and record access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for postmarketing adverse drug experience reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Key definitions: 'Adverse drug experience' (any adverse event associated with drug use in humans), 'Individual case safety report (ICSR)' (description of ADE related to an individual), 'ICSR attachments' (related documents like medical records), 'Disability' (substantial disruption of normal life functions), 'Life‑threatening adverse drug experience' (places patient at immediate risk of death as it occurred), 'Serious adverse drug experience' (results in death, life‑threat, hospitalization/prolongation, persistent/significant disability/incapacity, congenital anomaly/birth defect, or other events that may jeopardize patient require intervention), and 'Unexpected adverse drug experience' (not listed in current labeling or differs by greater severity or specificity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions to classify and determine reporting obligations (e.g., serious+unexpected triggers 15-day reports).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review obligation for adverse drug experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant with an approved application (or effective approved 505(b)(2) application) must promptly review all adverse drug experience information obtained or received from any source, foreign or domestic, including marketing experience, postmarketing clinical investigations, epidemiological studies, literature reports, and unpublished papers. Applicants must develop written procedures for surveillance, receipt, evaluation, and reporting of postmarketing ADEs to FDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish and follow documented pharmacovigilance procedures to ensure timely detection and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting format and electronic submission requirement for ADEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit adverse drug experience information to FDA as described in this section, and except as provided in paragraph (g)(2), these reports must be submitted in electronic format as described in paragraph (g)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow FDA electronic submission specifications unless an exception applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postmarketing 15‑day 'Alert reports' — triggers and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must report each adverse drug experience that is both serious and unexpected, domestic or foreign, as soon as possible but no later than 15 calendar days from initial receipt by the applicant. Follow-up reports must be submitted within 15 calendar days of receipt of new information or as requested by FDA. If a nonapplicant chooses to forward reports to the applicant rather than FDA, the nonapplicant must submit each such report to the applicant within 5 calendar days of initial receipt and keep records (copy of each report, dates received/submitted, and name/address of applicant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat serious+unexpected events as urgent; investigate promptly and submit initial and timely follow-up information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic adverse drug experience reporting schedule and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must report each ADE not reported as a 15‑day Alert at quarterly intervals for 3 years from approval, then annually. Quarterly reports must be submitted within 30 days of the close of the quarter (first quarter begins on date of approval); annual reports within 60 days of the anniversary of approval. FDA may extend or reestablish quarterly requirements or change timing. Follow-up info to ADEs submitted in a periodic report may be submitted in the next periodic report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain reporting calendar and incorporate follow-up data appropriately; watch for FDA notices altering reporting frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in each periodic report
rubrics_metrics.description: Each periodic report must contain: (A) descriptive information including (1) a narrative summary and analysis of report contents; (2) analysis of the 15‑day Alert reports submitted during the interval (referenced by patient ID code, adverse reaction terms, and submission date); (3) history of actions taken since last report because of ADEs (e.g., labeling changes, studies initiated); and (4) an index listing patient ID code and adverse reaction term(s) for all ICSRs submitted; and (B) ICSRs for all adverse drug experiences not reported as 15‑day Alerts (serious, expected, and nonserious) — submitted individually or in batches within the required timeframe. ICSRs must only be submitted once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide narrative analysis, cross-reference 15‑day reports, document actions taken, and include all applicable ICSRs (avoid duplicate ICSR submissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope exclusions for periodic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodic reporting (except for 15‑day Alerts) does not apply to ADE information obtained from postmarketing studies (whether or not under an IND), reports in the scientific literature, and foreign marketing experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle ADEs from postmarketing studies, literature, and foreign marketing under different reporting mechanisms as specified elsewhere; they are not included in periodic reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15‑day Alert reports based on scientific literature must include article copy
rubrics_metrics.description: A 15‑day Alert report based on information in the scientific literature must be accompanied by a copy of the published article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When literature triggers a 15‑day report, attach the publication to the submission.
